analysis.subject: civics
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers the census every 10 years on April 1 in years ending in zero, constitutional mandate in Article I and Title 13, first census in 1790 with 3,929,625 people and 105 seats among 15 states, growth to 435 seats in 1913, apportionment and redistricting uses, and 72 year confidentiality rule.

overview.headline: How the ten year census shapes House seats and district lines

keyPoints.point: The census is conducted every ten years on April 1 in years ending in zero.
keyPoints.quote: The U.S. Census Bureau conducts the census in years ending in zero, on Census Day, which is April 1.

keyPoints.point: Census data are used to apportion House seats among the states based on population.
keyPoints.quote: The data collected by the decennial census are used to apportion the number of seats each state has in the U.S. House of Representatives.

keyPoints.point: The Constitution directs that an enumeration be taken every ten years.
keyPoints.quote: The Constitution of the United States, Article I, Sections 2 and 9, directs that a census or enumeration be taken.

keyPoints.point: Redistricting occurs after each census when state officials redraw congressional district boundaries.
keyPoints.quote: Redistricting is when state officials redraw the boundaries of the congressional and state legislative districts in their states after each census.

keyTerms.gloss: dividing House seats among the states based on population figures
keyTerms.quote: Apportionment is the process of dividing the seats in the House of Representatives among the 50 states

keyTerms.gloss: process where state officials redraw district boundaries after population shifts
keyTerms.quote: Redistricting is when state officials redraw the boundaries of the congressional and state legislative districts in their states after each census.

keyTerms.gloss: census count that the Constitution directs be taken
keyTerms.quote: The Constitution of the United States, Article I, Sections 2 and 9, directs that a census or enumeration be taken.

keyTerms.gloss: census conducted every ten years to apportion seats based on collected population data
keyTerms.quote: The data collected by the decennial census are used to apportion the number of seats each state has in the U.S. House of Representatives.

keyTerms.gloss: federal law that requires congressional notification of census subjects years in advance
keyTerms.quote: Title 13 requires the Census Bureau to notify Congress of the planned subjects for the census no later than three years before that census

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Shows the ordered steps from notification deadlines to census day to apportionment to redistricting in taught order
componentPlan.focusQuote: Every 10 years, the U.S. Census Bureau conducts a census to determine the number of people living in the United States.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Contrasts the two post census processes that divide seats among states and redraw district lines
componentPlan.focusQuote: Apportionment is the process of dividing the seats in the House of Representatives among the 50 states
